# church-committee-book-ii-1976
- **URL:** https://www.intelligence.senate.gov/sites/default/files/94755_II.pdf (Final Report of the Select Committee to Study Governmental Operations with Respect to Intelligence Activities, Book II: "Intelligence Activities and the Rights of Americans," S. Rep. 94-755, April 1976; full 404-page PDF downloaded and searched) · **Accessed:** 2026-08-20 · **For:** v1 drafting, claims C28 (second source), C29, C30
- **What it establishes:** The Church Committee's own findings language on COINTELPRO, the MLK campaign, and cross-administration abuses; plus independent corroboration of Palmer Raids scale.
- **Key passages:**
  - COINTELPRO definition (Book II, p. 2): the third type of intelligence activity "is covert action designed to disrupt and discredit the activities of groups and individuals deemed a threat to the social order."
  - Findings (p. 10): "The FBI's COINTELPRO—counterintelligence program—was designed to 'disrupt' groups and 'neutralize' individuals deemed to be threats to domestic security... many of the tactics employed by the FBI were indisputably degrading to a free society."
  - White Hate directive language (1964, quoting FBI documents): a directive instituted a COINTELPRO against the Klan and "White Hate" organizations "to expose, disrupt, and otherwise neutralize" the activities of the groups, "their leaders, and adherents." (The five-word "expose, disrupt, misdirect, discredit, or otherwise neutralize" formulation is from the FBI's 1967 Black Nationalist COINTELPRO memo, quoted in Book III; Book II's own wording is as above — do not attribute the longer string to Book II.)
  - MLK (pp. 10–11): "From 'late 1963' until his death in 1968, Martin Luther King, Jr., was the target of an intensive campaign by the Federal Bureau of Investigation to 'neutralize' him as an effective civil rights leader. In the words of the man in charge of the FBI's 'war' against Dr. King, 'No holds were barred.'" Also: the FBI mailed King a hotel-microphone tape with a note "which Dr. King and his advisors interpreted as threatening to release the tape recording unless Dr. King committed suicide."
  - SCLC: FBI intensively investigated "the groups involved in protests against the Vietnam War and the civil rights movement, including Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr., and the Southern Christian Leadership Conference"; the Bureau rated its attempt to "put a stop" to a contribution to the SCLC "quite successful."
  - Program span: CPUSA COINTELPRO "formalized in 1956"; White Hate "1964–1971 period, when the program was in operation" (287 actions); "black nationalist" 1967–1971 (379 actions); "New Left" 1968–1971 (291 actions). Socialist Workers Party investigated "for more than three decades" despite the FBI's admission it "has committed no criminal acts."
  - C30 (both parties, FDR→Nixon): "It has become clear from our inquiry, moreover, that intelligence excesses, at home and abroad, have been found in every administration. They are not the product of any single party, administration, or man." (p. VIII) And Finding (i): "Each administration from Franklin D. Roosevelt's to Richard Nixon's permitted, and sometimes encouraged, government agencies to handle essentially political intelligence." (p. 9, with per-president examples Roosevelt→Nixon.)
  - Palmer Raids corroboration (p. 5): "Hundreds of American citizens were prosecuted for anti-war statements during World War I, and thousands of 'radical' aliens were seized for deportation during the 1920 Palmer Raids."
- **Reliability:** Primary (official Senate report, hosted by the Senate Intelligence Committee); the canonical source for COINTELPRO findings.
- **Relevance to this project:** C29 and C30 verbatim language; C28 second source; historical-precedent section.
